metadata.platform: ATLAS – Adaptive Tutoring and Learning System
metadata.note: Question bank for random selection by Freebuff. Curriculum-aligned to Ghana GES SHS 1 English Language.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes a conversation?
options: A one-way delivery of information from speaker to listener
A dynamic exchange of thoughts, ideas, and information between two or more people
A written message sent through the post
A formal speech delivered at a ceremony
questions.answer: A dynamic exchange of thoughts, ideas, and information between two or more people
questions.explanation: Conversation is a mutual, interactive process involving speaking, listening, responding, and turn-taking. It requires active participation from all parties.

questions.question: What does 'turn-taking' mean in a conversation?
options: One person speaks while the other is silent throughout
Alternating between speaking and listening roles during a conversation
Interrupting the other person whenever you have a point
Writing down your ideas before speaking
questions.answer: Alternating between speaking and listening roles during a conversation
questions.explanation: Turn-taking is the conversational practice of each participant taking a turn to speak, then listening while the other responds.

questions.question: Kofi and Ama are discussing how to solve a school project together. What TYPE of conversation is this?
questions.answer: Creative (brainstorming/problem-solving)
questions.explanation: A creative conversation involves brainstorming and problem-solving together.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of EFFECTIVE conversation?
options: Interrupting frequently to show you understand
Talking as much as possible to dominate the conversation
Active listening, empathy, and respectful tone
Using only formal language regardless of context
questions.answer: Active listening, empathy, and respectful tone
questions.explanation: Effective conversation requires active listening, empathy, and maintaining a respectful tone to build trust.

questions.question: A friend nods while you speak and says 'I see' after your point. What conversational role is your friend performing?
questions.answer: Providing feedback
questions.explanation: Feedback in conversation includes cues like nodding, 'I see', 'okay', or asking follow-up questions.

questions.question: A student talks to a school counsellor about personal worries. What type of conversation is this?
questions.answer: Therapeutic
questions.explanation: A therapeutic conversation involves counselling, emotional support, and helping someone process feelings.

questions.question: A trader tries to convince a customer to buy a product by giving reasons and benefits. What type of conversation is this?
questions.answer: Persuasive
questions.explanation: A persuasive conversation aims to convince or negotiate.

questions.question: What is the difference between a monologue and a dialogue?
options: A monologue involves two people; a dialogue involves one
A monologue is a speech by one person; a dialogue is an exchange between two or more people
A dialogue is always written; a monologue is always spoken
There is no difference between them
questions.answer: A monologue is a speech by one person; a dialogue is an exchange between two or more people
questions.explanation: A monologue is a long speech by one person. A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a good conversationalist?
options: Dominating the conversation without letting others speak
questions.answer: Dominating the conversation without letting others speak
questions.explanation: Good conversationalists are open-minded, empathetic, and allow others to speak.

questions.question: Two classmates chat about the weekend before class begins. What type of conversation is this?
questions.answer: Casual (small talk)
questions.explanation: Casual conversation (small talk) is light, informal chat that helps build social relationships.

questions.question: A teacher explains the causes of climate change to students. What type of conversation is happening?
questions.answer: Informative (sharing knowledge)
questions.explanation: An informative conversation focuses on sharing facts, knowledge, or explanations.

questions.question: In conversation, what does 'responding' mean?
options: Staying silent while the other person speaks
Reacting to and engaging with the other person's message
Writing down what the other person says
Changing the topic when you disagree
questions.answer: Reacting to and engaging with the other person's message
questions.explanation: Responding means reacting to the other person's message.

questions.question: What is the role of LISTENING in a conversation?
options: It is not important — only speaking matters
Paying full attention to the other person's messages to understand them
Looking away and thinking about your own response while they talk
Waiting for a pause to interrupt with your point
questions.answer: Paying full attention to the other person's messages to understand them
questions.explanation: Listening is foundational to communication.

questions.question: Four students share ideas and build on each other's suggestions to plan a presentation. This is an example of:
options: Dialogue — exchanging ideas and building on each other's thoughts
questions.answer: Dialogue — exchanging ideas and building on each other's thoughts
questions.explanation: Dialogue involves the back-and-forth exchange and building of ideas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of discourse?
questions.answer: Oral communication
questions.explanation: Discourse refers to communication — spoken or written.

questions.question: Why is it generally considered impolite to interrupt someone who is speaking?
options: Because the person may be saying something false
It disrupts turn-taking, shows disrespect, and prevents effective communication
Because it is always against school rules
Because it changes the topic of conversation
questions.answer: It disrupts turn-taking, shows disrespect, and prevents effective communication
questions.explanation: Interrupting breaks the turn-taking flow of conversation.

questions.question: A student listens to a long story and identifies the three most important events to retell. Which communication skill is this?
questions.answer: Summarising and identifying main ideas
questions.explanation: Summarising means extracting and retelling the most important points.

questions.question: Which of the following are elements of a story?
options: Plot, setting, characters, conflict, and point of view
questions.answer: Plot, setting, characters, conflict, and point of view
questions.explanation: The elements of a story are: plot, setting, characters, conflict, and point of view.

questions.question: What are the three main PARTS (structure) of a story?
questions.answer: Introduction, main body, and conclusion
questions.explanation: Every story has three structural parts: the introduction, the main body, and the conclusion.

questions.question: In the structure of a plot, what is the CLIMAX?
options: The introduction where characters are established
The most intense, critical moment where the outcome is decided
The final part where loose ends are tied up
The series of events leading to the main conflict
questions.answer: The most intense, critical moment where the outcome is decided
questions.explanation: The climax is the peak of a story — the turning point of greatest tension.

questions.question: In a story, the EXPOSITION is:
options: The series of complications building toward the climax
The introduction where setting, characters, and background are established
The resolution where the story ends
questions.answer: The introduction where setting, characters, and background are established
questions.explanation: The exposition opens a story by introducing the setting, characters, and background context.

questions.question: What is a SEQUEL in storytelling?
options: A summary of the original story
A continuation or follow-up of a previous story, often with the same characters
A character who appears only briefly in the main story
The climax scene of a narrative
questions.answer: A continuation or follow-up of a previous story, often with the same characters
questions.explanation: A sequel continues the narrative of a previous work.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of FORMAL language?
options: 'I would like to formally request your assistance with this matter.'
questions.answer: 'I would like to formally request your assistance with this matter.'
questions.explanation: Formal language is polite, structured, and avoids slang or contractions.

questions.question: Kwame is writing to his headmaster to request permission to leave school early. Which language type should he use?
options: Informal — it is just his headmaster
Formal — writing to an authority figure requires professional, respectful language
Pidgin English — it is easier to understand
questions.answer: Formal — writing to an authority figure requires professional, respectful language
questions.explanation: When communicating with authority figures, formal language is required.

questions.question: Ama texts her best friend: 'Can't wait 4 the party tonite! 😊'. This is an example of:
questions.answer: Informal language
questions.explanation: Informal language is used in casual, personal communication between friends and family.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST polite and formal way to ask for a pen?
options: 'Could you please lend me your pen?'
questions.answer: 'Could you please lend me your pen?'
questions.explanation: Polite, formal requests use indirect phrasing and the word 'please'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of formal language?
options: Using full forms of words instead of contractions
questions.answer: Using abbreviated words and emojis
questions.explanation: Formal language avoids abbreviations, contractions, slang, and emojis.

questions.question: A student is selected to speak at the morning school assembly about environmental cleanliness. What language style should they use?
options: Informal — to be relatable to fellow students
Formal — it is a public, official school occasion
Pidgin — because students understand it better
questions.answer: Formal — it is a public, official school occasion
questions.explanation: School assembly is a formal occasion requiring formal language.

questions.question: In formal writing, why should contractions like 'can't', 'won't', and 'I'm' be avoided?
options: Contractions are features of informal language; formal writing uses full forms like 'cannot', 'will not', 'I am'
They are only allowed in mathematics
questions.answer: Contractions are features of informal language; formal writing uses full forms like 'cannot', 'will not', 'I am'
questions.explanation: Contractions are casual and conversational. Formal writing requires full forms.

questions.question: You are introducing yourself to a new teacher. Which greeting is MOST appropriate?
options: 'Good morning, sir/madam. My name is Kofi Mensah. It is a pleasure to meet you.'
questions.answer: 'Good morning, sir/madam. My name is Kofi Mensah. It is a pleasure to meet you.'
questions.explanation: When addressing a teacher, formal language is required.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate formal apology?
options: 'I sincerely apologise for my tardiness and assure you it will not happen again.'
questions.answer: 'I sincerely apologise for my tardiness and assure you it will not happen again.'
questions.explanation: Formal apologies use complete sentences, polite vocabulary, and a commitment to improvement.

questions.question: Which feature makes an informal letter DIFFERENT from a formal letter?
options: An informal letter has no greeting
An informal letter uses a chatty tone, contractions, and friendly language
An informal letter always discusses official business
An informal letter has no address or date
questions.answer: An informal letter uses a chatty tone, contractions, and friendly language
questions.explanation: Informal letters are personal and conversational.

questions.question: The same student uses different language talking to his friend and to his principal. What principle of communication does this demonstrate?
options: That language varies according to context and the relationship between speaker and listener
That English is a difficult language
questions.answer: That language varies according to context and the relationship between speaker and listener
questions.explanation: Register changes based on who you are talking to, the setting, and the purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following occasions REQUIRES formal language?
options: Chatting with your best friend at break time
Delivering a speech at a prize-giving ceremony
questions.answer: Delivering a speech at a prize-giving ceremony
questions.explanation: Prize-giving ceremonies, debates, official meetings require formal language.

questions.question: What is a rhetorical question?
options: A question that requires a detailed written answer
A question that does not require an answer but is used to make a point or provoke reflection
A question asked in a mathematics examination
A question you ask when you genuinely do not know the answer
questions.answer: A question that does not require an answer but is used to make a point or provoke reflection
questions.explanation: Rhetorical questions are used in formal speeches to engage the audience.

questions.question: A student debater says: 'As Kwegyir Aggrey once said, if you educate a woman, you educate a whole nation.' Why is using a quotation effective in a formal speech?
options: Quotations add authority, credibility, and support to the argument
It replaces the need for your own ideas
It makes the speech informal and entertaining
questions.answer: Quotations add authority, credibility, and support to the argument
questions.explanation: Using quotations from respected figures strengthens arguments.

questions.question: Why is slang or pidgin English considered inappropriate in formal communication?
options: Because it is used only in Ghana
Slang and pidgin are informal expressions that lack the precision and professionalism required in formal settings
questions.answer: Slang and pidgin are informal expressions that lack the precision and professionalism required in formal settings
questions.explanation: Formal communication requires precise, universally understood language.

questions.question: Abena is preparing for a job interview. She should use language that is:
options: Very casual and relaxed to seem friendly
Full of slang to show personality
Mainly pidgin English to seem relatable
questions.answer: Formal, polite, and professional
questions.explanation: A job interview is a formal, professional context.

questions.question: An informal letter written to an older relative (like an uncle or aunt) is described as:
questions.answer: Semi-formal
questions.explanation: A semi-formal letter is between formal and informal.

questions.question: A speaker says: 'Studies show that 7 out of 10 Ghanaian students lack access to textbooks.' Why is using statistics effective in formal communication?
options: It makes the speech more entertaining
Statistics provide evidence, quantify arguments, and enhance credibility in formal contexts
It replaces the need for a conclusion
It is required by law in all speeches
questions.answer: Statistics provide evidence, quantify arguments, and enhance credibility in formal contexts
questions.explanation: In formal language, statistics are used to support arguments with numerical evidence.

questions.question: Match the situation with the correct language type: 'Sending an email to your school principal about a problem in the dormitory.'
options: Formal — the recipient is an authority figure in an official context
Slang — to keep the email short
questions.answer: Formal — the recipient is an authority figure in an official context
questions.explanation: An email to a principal is official correspondence.

questions.question: Which of these pairs shows the correct FORMAL equivalent of an informal expression? Informal: 'I wanna go home.'
questions.answer: 'I want to go home.' (formal)
questions.explanation: 'Wanna' is an informal contraction of 'want to'. The formal equivalent uses complete word forms.

questions.question: A student participating in a school debate uses phrases like 'Furthermore, it is my contention that...' and 'With all due respect to my opponent...'. This demonstrates:
options: Formal language use appropriate for a debate context
The use of slang in an argument
questions.answer: Formal language use appropriate for a debate context
questions.explanation: Debates are formal events requiring structured, polite, and professional language.

questions.question: Which of the following digital communication tools is typically used for FORMAL communication?
options: A professional email to a university admissions office
questions.answer: A professional email to a university admissions office
questions.explanation: Email to an official institution is formal communication.

questions.question: Which is the correct salutation for an informal letter to a friend named Adjoa?
questions.answer: Dear Adjoa,
questions.explanation: Informal letters to friends use first names in the salutation.

questions.question: What are paralinguistic features of communication?
options: Only the words spoken in a conversation
Aspects of communication that accompany spoken language but are not part of the verbal message itself — like gestures, facial expressions, and tone
The grammar rules of spoken English
The written version of a spoken conversation
questions.answer: Aspects of communication that accompany spoken language but are not part of the verbal message itself — like gestures, facial expressions, and tone
questions.explanation: Paralinguistic features are non-verbal elements that add meaning to speech.

questions.question: A speaker nods while their friend talks about a problem. What does this paralinguistic feature communicate?
options: Disagreement with what is being said
questions.answer: Active listening and agreement/acknowledgement
questions.explanation: Nodding signals agreement, acknowledgement, and active listening.

questions.question: Which of the following is a PLOSIVE consonant sound?
questions.answer: /p/ as in 'pet'
questions.explanation: Plosives are sounds made by completely stopping the flow of air and suddenly releasing it.

questions.question: Which of the following is a FRICATIVE consonant sound?
questions.answer: /f/ as in 'fine'
questions.explanation: Fricatives are sounds made by directing air through a narrow channel, creating friction.

questions.question: What does VOICING mean in the context of speech sounds?
options: The volume at which you speak
The presence or absence of vibration of the vocal cords when producing a sound
The choice of words in a conversation
questions.answer: The presence or absence of vibration of the vocal cords when producing a sound
questions.explanation: Voicing refers to whether the vocal cords vibrate when producing a sound.

questions.question: The sounds /p/ and /b/ are both plosives made at the same place in the mouth. What makes them DIFFERENT?
options: They are made at different places in the mouth
They are produced in exactly the same way
questions.answer: /b/ is voiced and /p/ is voiceless
questions.explanation: /b/ has vocal cord vibration (voiced) while /p/ does not (voiceless).

questions.question: What does 'place of articulation' refer to in phonics?
options: The emotion conveyed when the sound is produced
The points in the mouth or speech organs involved in producing a sound
The speed at which sounds are produced
questions.answer: The points in the mouth or speech organs involved in producing a sound
questions.explanation: Place of articulation refers to where in the mouth a sound is produced.

questions.question: What does 'manner of articulation' describe?
options: How a sound is produced — the method used to create it
Where in the mouth a sound is produced
The meaning of the sound in context
questions.answer: How a sound is produced — the method used to create it
questions.explanation: Manner of articulation describes HOW a sound is made.

questions.question: Maintaining eye contact while speaking to someone in a conversation signals:
options: Confidence, engagement, and respect for the listener
Desire to end the conversation quickly
questions.answer: Confidence, engagement, and respect for the listener
questions.explanation: Eye contact shows confidence, engagement, and respect.

questions.question: A teacher frowns deeply while a student gives an answer. What might this facial expression communicate?
options: Complete agreement with the student's answer
Confusion, concern, or disapproval without using any words
questions.answer: Confusion, concern, or disapproval without using any words
questions.explanation: Facial expressions are powerful paralinguistic features.

questions.question: How many plosive consonant sounds does English have?
questions.explanation: English has six plosive sounds: /p/, /b/, /t/, /d/, /k/, /g/.

questions.question: A student raises their hand in class before speaking. This gesture communicates:
options: That the student wants to leave the class
That the student is requesting permission to contribute to the discussion
That the student disagrees with the teacher
questions.answer: That the student is requesting permission to contribute to the discussion
questions.explanation: Raising a hand is a learned, culturally agreed gesture.

questions.question: A mother says 'Well done' to her child in a flat, uninterested tone. What does this tell us about communication?
options: Tone of voice does not matter — the words are positive
Tone of voice and manner of delivery can completely change the meaning of the words spoken
The child definitely did a good job
The mother is using formal language
questions.answer: Tone of voice and manner of delivery can completely change the meaning of the words spoken
questions.explanation: Tone, pitch, and pace modify meaning.

questions.question: In which word is the fricative sound /ʃ/ (as in 'show') used?
questions.answer: rush
questions.explanation: The /ʃ/ fricative appears in: show, push, rush, fresh, dish.

questions.question: Which word contains the fricative sound /dʒ/ (as in 'joke')?
questions.answer: large
questions.explanation: The /dʒ/ sound appears in words like joke, damage, large, and judge.

questions.question: A student stands upright, makes eye contact, and uses open hand gestures while presenting. What does this body language communicate?
options: Confidence, openness, and engagement with the audience
questions.answer: Confidence, openness, and engagement with the audience
questions.explanation: Upright posture signals confidence and preparedness.

questions.question: In connected speech, what happens to sounds when words flow together naturally?
options: Every word is spoken at the same pace with equal stress
Sounds may link, reduce, or change slightly at word boundaries to make speech flow more naturally
All words are pronounced exactly as they are written
Connected speech is always slower than reading aloud
questions.answer: Sounds may link, reduce, or change slightly at word boundaries to make speech flow more naturally
questions.explanation: In natural connected speech, sounds link and change at word boundaries.

questions.question: A student is giving a speech at the National Science and Maths Quiz. Which combination of features will make their delivery most effective?
options: Mumbling, looking at the floor, speaking very fast
Clear pronunciation, appropriate pace, good posture, and eye contact with the audience
Only using loud volume throughout the speech
Reading word-for-word from a paper without looking up
questions.answer: Clear pronunciation, appropriate pace, good posture, and eye contact with the audience
questions.explanation: Effective public speaking combines verbal and paralinguistic elements.

questions.question: When you move very close to someone during a conversation and they step back, they are communicating through:
questions.answer: Non-verbal/paralinguistic communication (personal space preference)
questions.explanation: Personal space is a paralinguistic/non-verbal feature.

questions.question: A student speaks very softly at a school debate and the audience cannot hear. What paralinguistic feature needs improvement?
questions.answer: Voice projection and volume
questions.explanation: Voice projection is an essential paralinguistic feature for public speaking.

questions.question: A skilled speaker pauses for 3 seconds before announcing an important point. What effect does this deliberate pause create?
options: It shows the speaker has forgotten what to say
It creates anticipation and draws the audience's attention to what follows
It signals the end of the speech
It is a sign of nervousness
questions.answer: It creates anticipation and draws the audience's attention to what follows
questions.explanation: Strategic pauses are powerful paralinguistic tools.

questions.question: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.' Which sound is being practised in this tongue twister?
questions.answer: The plosive /p/
questions.explanation: Peter, Piper, picked, peck, peppers — all begin with the bilabial plosive /p/.

questions.question: What does it mean to understand a word 'in context'?
options: Memorising the dictionary definition without knowing when to use it
Using the surrounding text, situation, and register to understand the meaning and appropriate use of a word
Writing the word in a sentence from a textbook
questions.answer: Using the surrounding text, situation, and register to understand the meaning and appropriate use of a word
questions.explanation: Understanding vocabulary in context means using clues from the surrounding text.

questions.question: Which word is a SYNONYM for 'happy'?
questions.answer: Joyful
questions.explanation: Synonyms are words with the same or similar meaning.

questions.question: Which word is an ANTONYM for 'formal'?
questions.answer: Informal
questions.explanation: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings.

questions.question: A student writes: 'The man walked slowly.' Which word MOST precisely describes someone walking very slowly due to tiredness?
questions.answer: Trudged
questions.explanation: 'Trudged' means to walk slowly and heavily, typically due to exhaustion.

questions.question: Which word is MORE appropriate in a formal written context? 'The company will _____ its old equipment.'
questions.answer: dispose of
questions.explanation: 'Dispose of' is formal vocabulary.

questions.question: In a story, the word 'protagonist' refers to:
options: The villain or antagonist of the story
The main character around whom the story revolves
questions.answer: The main character around whom the story revolves
questions.explanation: The protagonist is the main character of a story.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the article CORRECTLY?
options: I saw a orange on the table.
He bought a umbrella from a shop.
They have a hour to finish.
questions.answer: She is an honest person.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before words beginning with a vowel SOUND. 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h'.

questions.question: The words 'slim', 'slender', and 'skinny' all mean thin. Which has a NEGATIVE connotation?
questions.answer: Skinny
questions.explanation: 'Skinny' has a negative connotation — it implies being unhealthily thin.

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'The teacher commended the students for their exemplary behaviour.' What does 'commended' mean?
questions.answer: Praised and expressed approval
questions.explanation: 'Commended' means to formally praise or express approval.

questions.question: What is a BIOGRAPHY?
options: A story made up by the imagination of the writer
An account of a real person's life written by someone else
A formal letter to a government official
questions.answer: An account of a real person's life written by someone else
questions.explanation: A biography is a non-fiction text — the written account of a real person's life.

questions.question: Which phrase most precisely and formally describes the action in: 'The company ended the project.'?
options: The company finished off the project
The company stopped the project dead
questions.answer: The company terminated the project
questions.explanation: 'Terminated' is the most formal and precise verb here.

questions.question: Words like 'furthermore', 'however', 'in addition', and 'therefore' are called:
questions.answer: Linking words or cohesive devices
questions.explanation: Linking words connect ideas within and between sentences.

questions.question: 'The new student was very gregarious — she made friends with everyone on her first day.' What does 'gregarious' mean?
questions.answer: Sociable and fond of company
questions.explanation: The context clue 'made friends with everyone' tells us 'gregarious' means sociable.

questions.question: What is a MEMO (memorandum)?
options: A formal communication or notification that operates within an organisation
An informal letter to a friend
questions.answer: A formal communication or notification that operates within an organisation
questions.explanation: A memo is a formal internal document used within organisations.

questions.question: What is an AGENDA in the context of meetings and communication?
options: A summary written after a meeting
A list or outline of things to be considered, discussed, or done at a meeting
A type of formal letter sent to the public
questions.answer: A list or outline of things to be considered, discussed, or done at a meeting
questions.explanation: An agenda is prepared before a meeting and lists all items to be discussed.

questions.question: 'Communicate', 'communication', 'communicative', 'communicator' — these words all belong to the same:
questions.answer: Word family
questions.explanation: A word family shares the same root.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches an INFORMAL word with its FORMAL equivalent?
questions.answer: Get (informal) → Obtain (formal)
questions.explanation: 'Get' is informal; 'obtain' or 'acquire' are formal equivalents.

questions.question: What is SKIMMING as a reading strategy?
options: Reading every word carefully to understand details
Reading quickly to get the general idea or main topic of a text
Reading only the last paragraph of a text
questions.answer: Reading quickly to get the general idea or main topic of a text
questions.explanation: Skimming is a rapid reading technique used to get a general overview.

questions.question: What is SCANNING as a reading strategy?
options: Reading every word slowly and carefully
Reading quickly to find specific information or a particular word/fact
Reading to understand the emotions in a text
questions.answer: Reading quickly to find specific information or a particular word/fact
questions.explanation: Scanning is searching a text quickly for specific information.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a NON-FICTION text?
options: A novel about a dragon in ancient Ghana
A fairy tale about a magic river
A biography of Dr Kwame Nkrumah
A poem about an imaginary forest
questions.answer: A biography of Dr Kwame Nkrumah
questions.explanation: Non-fiction texts are based on real facts, events, and people.

questions.question: Before reading a text, a student looks at the title, pictures, and headings to guess what it will be about. This strategy is called:
questions.answer: Prediction
questions.explanation: Prediction uses available clues to anticipate content.

questions.question: The sentence reads: 'The principal was adamant that all students must wear their uniforms.' What does 'adamant' mean?
options: Extremely firm and unwilling to change one's mind
questions.answer: Extremely firm and unwilling to change one's mind
questions.explanation: 'Adamant' means absolutely firm and determined.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the FORMAT of an informal letter?
options: Address and date at the top, Dear + first name, chatty body, friendly closing
Begin with 'To Whom It May Concern'
questions.answer: Address and date at the top, Dear + first name, chatty body, friendly closing
questions.explanation: An informal letter format includes address, date, salutation, body, and friendly closing.

questions.question: An ARTICLE written for a school magazine should have which of the following features?
options: No title, just the writer's name at the top
A bold, underlined title, an introduction, a main body with paragraphs, a conclusion, and the writer's subscription
A memo heading and reference number
questions.answer: A bold, underlined title, an introduction, a main body with paragraphs, a conclusion, and the writer's subscription
questions.explanation: An article has: a clear title, introduction, main body, conclusion, and subscription.

questions.question: Which type of article EXPLAINS a complex topic clearly and precisely for the reader?
questions.answer: Expository article
questions.explanation: An expository article explains a topic clearly and precisely.

questions.question: A student writes an article titled 'Why Ghana Must Invest More in Science Education' and argues for this position using evidence. This is a:
questions.answer: Persuasive article
questions.explanation: A persuasive article takes a clear position and uses arguments to convince the reader.

questions.question: When sending a formal email to a university admissions office, what should you include in the 'Subject' line?
options: Nothing — the subject line is optional
A clear, brief description of the reason for your email
questions.answer: A clear, brief description of the reason for your email
questions.explanation: The subject line tells the recipient what the email is about.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a MEMO (memorandum)?
options: To write a personal letter to a friend
To publish an article in a newspaper
To communicate formally within an organisation for day-to-day business
To write a fictional story for a school magazine
questions.answer: To communicate formally within an organisation for day-to-day business
questions.explanation: A memo is an internal formal document used within organisations.

questions.question: When writing a formal letter of application for a job, which salutation is correct if you do NOT know the recipient's name?
options: To Whom It May Concern, / Dear Sir or Madam,
questions.answer: To Whom It May Concern, / Dear Sir or Madam,
questions.explanation: When the recipient's name is unknown, use 'To Whom It May Concern' or 'Dear Sir or Madam'.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an INTRODUCTORY paragraph in an essay?
options: To provide the conclusion of the argument
To identify or state the main idea to be discussed in the essay
To list all the supporting evidence
questions.answer: To identify or state the main idea to be discussed in the essay
questions.explanation: The introductory paragraph introduces the topic and states the main idea.

questions.question: What is the role of BODY PARAGRAPHS in an essay?
options: To introduce the main topic for the first time
To provide supporting details, evidence, and development of the main idea
To conclude and summarise all points made
To list the sources used in the essay
questions.answer: To provide supporting details, evidence, and development of the main idea
questions.explanation: Body paragraphs develop specific supporting points with evidence.

questions.question: A concluding paragraph in an essay should:
options: Introduce new information not mentioned before
Repeat the introduction word for word
Summarise the main points discussed and provide a satisfying close
questions.answer: Summarise the main points discussed and provide a satisfying close
questions.explanation: A conclusion sums up key points and brings the piece to a close.

questions.question: At the bottom right of a newspaper article, the writer puts their name and position. This is called:
questions.answer: The subscription
questions.explanation: The subscription is the writer's identification at the bottom right of the article.

questions.question: Which type of article TELLS a story or narrates an event in a creative and engaging way?
questions.answer: Narrative article
questions.explanation: A narrative article tells a story in an engaging, story-like way.

questions.question: A journalist writes a detailed article about the atmosphere at Kejetia Market — the sights, sounds, and smells. This is best described as a:
questions.answer: Descriptive article
questions.explanation: A descriptive article describes a topic in detail, creating a clear picture.

questions.question: Articles are written for publication in newspapers and magazines mainly to:
options: Keep them private for the writer's personal use
Educate, inform, and entertain a public audience on relevant topics
questions.answer: Educate, inform, and entertain a public audience on relevant topics
questions.explanation: Published articles reach a broad audience to inform, educate, or entertain.

questions.question: When applying for a job via email, what document is usually ATTACHED?
options: A curriculum vitae (CV) with background and qualifications
An informal letter to a friend
questions.answer: A curriculum vitae (CV) with background and qualifications
questions.explanation: A CV provides employers with detailed information about qualifications and experience.

questions.question: In a school prefects' meeting, the agenda includes items to be discussed. What is the PURPOSE of an agenda?
options: To write the minutes of the meeting
To list and organise what will be discussed at the meeting
questions.answer: To list and organise what will be discussed at the meeting
questions.explanation: An agenda lists items to be discussed and keeps the meeting focused.

questions.question: What is a LINEAR NARRATIVE essay?
options: A story told in a random, non-chronological order
An essay that uses appropriate linking words to show relationships between ideas and sentences in a logical order
A poem that tells a story
questions.answer: An essay that uses appropriate linking words to show relationships between ideas and sentences in a logical order
questions.explanation: A linear narrative uses linking words to connect ideas in a logical order.

questions.question: In a school play, one character speaks alone on stage for a long time, revealing their thoughts. This is called a:
questions.answer: Monologue
questions.explanation: A monologue is a long speech delivered by one person.

questions.question: Two students write a play script where their characters argue. Their back-and-forth exchange is:
questions.answer: A dialogue
questions.explanation: A dialogue is a written or spoken exchange between two or more people.

questions.question: Which closing is appropriate for an informal letter to a friend?
questions.answer: Your friend, / With love,
questions.explanation: Informal letters close with warm, personal sign-offs like 'Your friend' or 'With love'.

questions.question: According to the curriculum, letters in the digital age have evolved to include:
options: Emails, text messages, social media messages, and online forum posts
Only letters printed on official letterhead
questions.answer: Emails, text messages, social media messages, and online forum posts
questions.explanation: Digital communication has expanded the concept of 'letter' to include many forms.

questions.question: Match the text type to its purpose: 'A student writes to the school to formally complain about poor sanitation in the dormitory.'
options: Informal letter — a complaint is always personal
Formal letter — an official complaint to an institution requires formal language and structure
A memo — complaints are internal documents
An article — complaints should be published
questions.answer: Formal letter — an official complaint to an institution requires formal language and structure
questions.explanation: Complaints to institutions are formal correspondence.

questions.question: What is an ADJECTIVE?
options: A word that describes an action
A word that describes or modifies a noun
A word that connects two clauses
A word that shows the position of an object
questions.answer: A word that describes or modifies a noun
questions.explanation: Adjectives describe nouns by providing more information about them.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The tall boy won the race', what type of adjective is 'tall'?
questions.answer: Attributive adjective
questions.explanation: An attributive adjective comes BEFORE the noun it describes.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The market is busy', what type of adjective is 'busy'?
questions.answer: Predicative adjective
questions.explanation: A predicative adjective comes AFTER a linking verb.

questions.question: Which of the following is a LINKING VERB?
questions.answer: Seems
questions.explanation: Linking verbs connect the subject to a predicative adjective or noun.

questions.question: What are the THREE degrees of comparison for adjectives?
questions.answer: Positive, comparative, and superlative
questions.explanation: Adjectives have three degrees: positive, comparative, and superlative.

questions.question: What is the COMPARATIVE form of the adjective 'bright'?
questions.answer: Brighter
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjectives form the comparative by adding '-er'.

questions.question: What is the SUPERLATIVE form of the adjective 'intelligent'?
questions.answer: Most intelligent
questions.explanation: Adjectives with three or more syllables use 'most' + adjective.

questions.question: What is the comparative and superlative of the adjective 'good'?
questions.answer: Better, best
questions.explanation: 'Good' is irregular: good → better → best.

questions.question: What happens to the spelling of a short adjective ending in a single vowel + consonant when you add '-er' or '-est'?
options: You just add '-er' or '-est' without any change
You double the final consonant before adding '-er' or '-est'
questions.answer: You double the final consonant before adding '-er' or '-est'
questions.explanation: Big → bigger → biggest; hot → hotter → hottest.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of the adjective 'happy'?
questions.answer: Happier
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in consonant + 'y' change the 'y' to 'i' before adding '-er'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the COMPARATIVE degree CORRECTLY?
options: Ama is the tallest girl in the class.
She is the more clever student in school.
He runs the fastest than everyone.
questions.answer: Kofi is taller than Kwame.
questions.explanation: Comparatives compare TWO things and use 'than'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the SUPERLATIVE degree CORRECTLY?
options: She is smarter than her sister.
He is the most hardworking student in the entire school.
This book is more interesting than that one.
She is the more intelligent of the two.
questions.answer: He is the most hardworking student in the entire school.
questions.explanation: Superlatives compare one thing with a group of THREE or more.

questions.question: Identify the adjective(s) in this sentence: 'The diligent students received excellent grades.'
questions.answer: diligent, excellent
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' describes 'students' and 'excellent' describes 'grades'.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Accra is a busy city', 'busy' is in the:
questions.answer: Positive (base) degree
questions.explanation: The positive degree is the basic, uncompared form of an adjective.

questions.question: Which sentence has the adjective in the WRONG position?
questions.answer: He is tired very.
questions.explanation: 'Very' is an adverb that must PRECEDE the adjective.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The soup tastes delicious', what type of adjective is 'delicious' and what type of verb is 'tastes'?
questions.answer: Predicative adjective; linking verb
questions.explanation: 'Tastes' is a linking verb: 'delicious' follows it and describes the subject 'soup'.

questions.question: What is the SUPERLATIVE form of the adjective 'bad'?
questions.answer: Worst
questions.explanation: 'Bad' is irregular: bad → worse → worst.

questions.question: In the sentence 'These three red mangoes are ripe', how many adjectives (attributive) are there?
questions.explanation: 'These' (demonstrative), 'three' (numeral adjective), and 'red' (descriptive adjective) all describe 'mangoes'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the 'as ... as' construction for comparison?
options: Ama is as tall than Kofi.
Ama is as tall as Kofi.
Ama is more tall as Kofi.
questions.answer: Ama is as tall as Kofi.
questions.explanation: 'As + adjective + as' shows equality between two things.

questions.question: A student observes: 'Abena is the cleverest girl in Form One.' This uses the superlative correctly because:
options: It compares Abena to one other girl
It compares Abena to ALL girls in Form One (a group of more than two)
questions.answer: It compares Abena to ALL girls in Form One (a group of more than two)
questions.explanation: Superlatives compare one member to all others in a group of three or more.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct form: 'Of the two brothers, Kwesi is the _____ student.'
questions.answer: more hardworking
questions.explanation: When comparing exactly TWO things, use the comparative.

questions.question: Why should writers avoid using too many adjectives in a single sentence?
options: Too many adjectives make sentences heavy, cluttered, and harder to read
Adjectives should never be used in writing
Only verbs are allowed in good writing
questions.answer: Too many adjectives make sentences heavy, cluttered, and harder to read
questions.explanation: One or two precise, vivid adjectives are more effective than a string of vague ones.

questions.question: Which sentence is written MORE correctly? a) 'She is more prettier than her friend.' b) 'She is prettier than her friend.'
options: Sentence a) — 'more prettier' is the superlative
Sentence b) — 'prettier' is already the comparative; 'more' creates a double comparative error
questions.answer: Sentence b) — 'prettier' is already the comparative; 'more' creates a double comparative error
questions.explanation: 'More prettier' is a double comparative — a common grammar error.

questions.question: What is TENSE in grammar?
options: The emotion expressed by a sentence
The form of the verb that shows when an action takes place
The degree of comparison of an adjective
questions.answer: The form of the verb that shows when an action takes place
questions.explanation: Tense locates an action in time: past, present, or future.

questions.question: What does ASPECT show about a verb?
options: The time at which an action occurs
How the action takes place over time — whether it is ongoing, completed, repeated, or habitual
The place where the action happens
questions.answer: How the action takes place over time — whether it is ongoing, completed, repeated, or habitual
questions.explanation: Aspect tells us HOW the action unfolds over time.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the SIMPLE PRESENT tense?
options: He will go to the market.
questions.answer: Kofi plays football every Saturday.
questions.explanation: Simple present expresses habitual, regular, or general truths.

questions.question: How is the SIMPLE PAST tense formed for regular verbs?
options: By adding '-ing' to the base form
By adding '-ed' to the base form
By placing 'will' before the base form
By adding 'has/have' before the past participle
questions.answer: By adding '-ed' to the base form
questions.explanation: Regular verbs form simple past by adding '-ed': walk → walked.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the PRESENT PROGRESSIVE (continuous) tense?
options: She was reading when I arrived.
She is reading a novel right now.
She has read the entire book.
questions.answer: She is reading a novel right now.
questions.explanation: Present progressive (is/am/are + '-ing') describes action in progress.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the PRESENT PERFECT tense?
options: I was eating when she called.
I have already eaten my lunch.
questions.answer: I have already eaten my lunch.
questions.explanation: Present perfect (has/have + past participle) connects past action to the present.

questions.question: What is the BASE FORM (infinitive) of a verb?
options: The unconjugated verb — the raw form without changes
The verb in the past tense
questions.answer: The unconjugated verb — the raw form without changes
questions.explanation: The base form is the unconjugated verb: walk, eat, write, be.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the SIMPLE FUTURE tense?
options: She cooks jollof rice on Fridays.
She will cook jollof rice tomorrow.
questions.answer: She will cook jollof rice tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Simple future uses 'will + base form'.

questions.question: What is the simple past form of the irregular verb 'go'?
questions.answer: Went
questions.explanation: 'Go' is irregular: go → went → gone.

questions.question: What is the PAST PARTICIPLE of the verb 'write'?
questions.answer: Written
questions.explanation: Past participle of 'write' is 'written'.

questions.question: Which tense is used to describe a HABITUAL or regular action?
questions.answer: Simple present
questions.explanation: Simple present describes habits, routines, and general truths.

questions.question: What is CONJUGATION of a verb?
options: Translating the verb to another language
Modifying a verb to indicate tense, aspect, person, and number
Adding an adjective before a verb
Replacing a verb with a noun
questions.answer: Modifying a verb to indicate tense, aspect, person, and number
questions.explanation: Conjugation changes a verb's form to match subject, tense, and aspect.

questions.question: What is the function of adding '-ing' to a verb in progressive tenses?
options: It makes the verb into a noun
It shows that an action is ongoing or in progress at a specific time
It shows that an action has been completed
It forms the past tense of the verb
questions.answer: It shows that an action is ongoing or in progress at a specific time
questions.explanation: The '-ing' form is used with 'be' verbs to form progressive tenses.

questions.question: A student writes a story about past events. Which tense should they mainly use?
questions.answer: Simple past tense
questions.explanation: Stories about past events use the simple past tense.

questions.question: Why is it important to maintain CONSISTENT tense in a piece of writing?
options: It is not important — you can switch tenses freely
Consistent tense helps readers follow the timeline clearly; switching tenses randomly causes confusion
Present tense is always better than past tense
Future tense should always be used in formal writing
questions.answer: Consistent tense helps readers follow the timeline clearly; switching tenses randomly causes confusion
questions.explanation: Tense consistency helps readers understand when events happen.

questions.question: Identify the verb in: 'The children are playing football in the school compound.'
questions.answer: are playing
questions.explanation: 'Are playing' is the verb phrase in present progressive form.

questions.question: Which of the following is a STATE verb (not an action)?
questions.answer: Know
questions.explanation: State verbs describe conditions rather than actions: know, believe, love.

questions.question: Which time expression is most commonly used with the PRESENT PERFECT tense?
options: Already, yet, just, ever, never, recently
questions.answer: Already, yet, just, ever, never, recently
questions.explanation: These are typical present perfect signal words.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the PAST PROGRESSIVE tense?
options: She goes to the market daily.
She was going to the market when it started raining.
She will go to the market.
questions.answer: She was going to the market when it started raining.
questions.explanation: Past progressive (was/were + '-ing') describes an ongoing action in the past.

questions.question: Which verb form is correct for the third person singular in the SIMPLE PRESENT tense?
questions.answer: He walks to school.
questions.explanation: Third person singular subjects require an '-s' ending.

questions.question: 'I have eaten, I am eating, I ate, I will eat' — these demonstrate:
options: Four different verb forms showing different tenses and aspects of 'eat'
questions.answer: Four different verb forms showing different tenses and aspects of 'eat'
questions.explanation: These are different tense/aspect forms of the same verb 'eat'.

questions.question: A student writes a diary entry: 'Today I wake up early and go to school.' What is the error?
options: Past tense should be used: 'Today I woke up early and went to school.'
questions.answer: Past tense should be used: 'Today I woke up early and went to school.'
questions.explanation: Diary entries recount events that have already happened, so past tense is correct.

questions.question: What is a DETERMINER?
options: A word that describes an action
A word placed before a noun to clarify its quantity, possession, or specificity
A word that connects two sentences
A word that shows the degree of an adjective
questions.answer: A word placed before a noun to clarify its quantity, possession, or specificity
questions.explanation: Determiners include articles, possessives, demonstratives, and quantifiers.

questions.question: When do you use the DEFINITE ARTICLE 'the'?
options: Before any noun at the start of a sentence
When referring to something specific or already known
Before all nouns that begin with a vowel
questions.answer: When referring to something specific or already known
questions.explanation: 'The' refers to a specific noun known to both speaker and listener.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the indefinite article CORRECTLY?
options: They saw a elephant at the zoo.
It is a honour to meet you.
questions.answer: She has an idea.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before a vowel SOUND.

questions.question: Which of the following are DEMONSTRATIVE determiners?
questions.answer: this, that, these, those
questions.explanation: Demonstrative determiners point to specific nouns.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Their house is near the school', what type of determiner is 'their'?
questions.answer: Possessive determiner
questions.explanation: Possessive determiners (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) show ownership.

questions.question: Which of the following is a QUANTIFIER?
questions.answer: All
questions.explanation: Quantifiers express amount or quantity: all, some, many, few.

questions.question: What is a PREPOSITION?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word that connects a noun/pronoun to other words to show their relationship
A word that expresses strong emotion
A word that replaces a noun
questions.answer: A word that connects a noun/pronoun to other words to show their relationship
questions.explanation: Prepositions show relationships of place, time, direction, and manner.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a preposition of PLACE correctly?
options: The cat is between the 5 o'clock.
The book is on the shelf.
questions.answer: The book is on the shelf.
questions.explanation: 'On' is a preposition of place showing position in relation to the shelf.

questions.question: 'She walked _____ the school gate and then _____ the road.' Which prepositions complete this?
questions.answer: through, across
questions.explanation: 'Through' for an enclosed space; 'across' for a surface.

questions.question: Which preposition correctly completes: 'We will see each other _____ the holidays'?
questions.answer: during
questions.explanation: 'During' is a preposition of time for events within a defined period.

questions.question: What is an INTERJECTION?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word used to connect two clauses
A word or phrase used to express a sudden, strong emotion
A word that shows the action of a verb
questions.answer: A word or phrase used to express a sudden, strong emotion
questions.explanation: Interjections express sudden feelings: Wow!, Ouch!, Hooray!

questions.question: A student arrives and the prefect says 'Akwaaba!' What function does this serve?
options: It expresses a warm welcome and greeting
questions.answer: It expresses a warm welcome and greeting
questions.explanation: 'Akwaaba' is a Ghanaian interjection meaning 'welcome'.

questions.question: How is a strong interjection punctuated?
questions.answer: With an exclamation mark (!)
questions.explanation: Strong interjections are followed by an exclamation mark.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'between' and 'among' correctly?
options: Share the bread between the three friends.
Share the bread among the two of you.
Share the bread between the entire school.
The secret is among the two sisters.
questions.answer: Share the bread among the two of you.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for three or more; 'between' is for exactly two.

questions.mission_title: The In vs On vs At
questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct preposition of TIME?
questions.answer: I was born in 2006.
questions.explanation: 'In' for years, months, seasons; 'on' for days; 'at' for specific times.

questions.question: In the sentence: 'All the learners completed every task', how many determiners are there?
questions.explanation: 'All', 'the', and 'every' are the determiners.

questions.question: In 'The students sat under the mango tree', 'under the mango tree' is a:
questions.answer: Prepositional phrase
questions.explanation: A prepositional phrase = preposition + noun phrase.

questions.question: Which interjection expresses PAIN or discomfort?
questions.answer: Ouch!
questions.explanation: 'Ouch!' expresses sudden pain or discomfort.

questions.question: Which sentence ends with a preposition ACCEPTABLY in modern English?
options: This is the kind of grammar up with which I will not put.
This is something I cannot agree with.
Prepositions at the end are always wrong.
End a sentence never with a preposition.
questions.answer: This is something I cannot agree with.
questions.explanation: Ending a sentence with a preposition is generally acceptable in modern English.

questions.question: What is a SENTENCE?
options: Any group of words written on a line
A group of words that expresses a complete thought, beginning with a capital and ending with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark
A phrase with only a verb
questions.answer: A group of words that expresses a complete thought
questions.explanation: A sentence is a grammatically complete unit of language.

questions.question: What is the SUBJECT of a sentence?
options: Who or what the sentence is about — usually the person or thing doing the action
The description of how the action is done
questions.answer: Who or what the sentence is about — usually the person or thing doing the action
questions.explanation: The subject is who or what the sentence is about.

questions.question: What is the PREDICATE of a sentence?
options: The noun that performs the action
The part that contains the verb and says something about the subject
The adjective that describes the subject
The word that introduces the sentence
questions.answer: The part that contains the verb and says something about the subject
questions.explanation: The predicate is everything in a sentence except the subject.

questions.question: Identify the SIMPLE SUBJECT in: 'The tall, smiling teacher entered the classroom.'
questions.answer: teacher
questions.explanation: The simple subject is the main noun without modifiers.

questions.question: Which sentence has a COMPOUND SUBJECT?
options: Kofi and Abena won the quiz competition.
questions.answer: Kofi and Abena won the quiz competition.
questions.explanation: A compound subject has two or more parts joined by a conjunction.

questions.question: When MUST a word begin with a capital letter?
options: First word of a sentence, and proper nouns
questions.answer: First word of a sentence, and proper nouns
questions.explanation: Capital letters: first word of sentence, proper nouns, titles.

questions.question: What type of sentence is: 'What an incredible performance by the students!'
questions.answer: Exclamatory sentence
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong emotion and end with '!'.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INTERROGATIVE sentence?
options: The book is on the desk.
questions.answer: Have you completed your assignment?
questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences ask questions and end with '?'.

questions.question: 'Please read the first paragraph aloud.' — What type of sentence is this?
questions.answer: Imperative
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences give commands, instructions, or requests.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT?
options: The group of students were making noise.
Each of the boys have a book.
Every student is expected to bring a pen.
questions.answer: Every student is expected to bring a pen.
questions.explanation: 'Every student' is singular, so it takes a singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark is used to show possession (ownership)?
questions.answer: Apostrophe (')
questions.explanation: An apostrophe shows possession: Kofi's book.

questions.question: 'Running through the market.' — Why is this a sentence FRAGMENT?
options: It expresses a complete thought correctly
It lacks a subject and complete predicate — it does not express a complete thought
questions.answer: It lacks a subject and complete predicate — it does not express a complete thought
questions.explanation: A fragment is an incomplete sentence lacking a subject or complete verb.

questions.question: Two simple sentences: 'Kofi was tired.' 'He continued studying.' — Combine into a COMPOUND sentence:
options: Kofi was tired, but he continued studying.
Kofi was tired he continued studying.
Kofi was tired because he continued studying.
Kofi tired was but he continued studying.
questions.answer: Kofi was tired, but he continued studying.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a comma + conjunction.

questions.question: In 'The boy who scored the highest mark in the exam will receive a prize', what is the SUBJECT?
options: The boy who scored the highest mark in the exam
questions.answer: The boy who scored the highest mark in the exam
questions.explanation: The subject includes the main noun and its modifier clause.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a QUESTION MARK?
options: I wonder if it will rain today?
She asked whether I had eaten?
He wants to know where you are going?
questions.answer: Did you complete the assignment?
questions.explanation: Question marks are only used with direct questions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a COMPLETE, correctly punctuated sentence?
options: The students studied hard and passed their exams.
Because she was late for the assembly.
questions.answer: The students studied hard and passed their exams.
questions.explanation: This has a subject, verb, and expresses a complete thought.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically CORRECT?
options: We don't have any homework today.
questions.answer: We don't have any homework today.
questions.explanation: 'Don't' with I, you, we, they; 'doesn't' with he, she, it.

questions.question: In which situation is an exclamation mark MOST appropriate?
options: At the end of every sentence to show emphasis
To express strong emotion: 'We won the championship!'
questions.answer: To express strong emotion: 'We won the championship!'
questions.explanation: Exclamation marks express strong emotion and should be used sparingly.

questions.question: Why is correct grammar important in communication?
options: Ensures your message is clear, accurate, and understood as intended
Does not matter as long as people guess what you mean
questions.answer: Ensures your message is clear, accurate, and understood as intended
questions.explanation: Good grammar helps you communicate clearly in any context.

questions.question: 'Each student in the three classes have submitted their project.' What is the error?
options: 'Have submitted' should be 'has submitted' — 'each' is singular
questions.answer: 'Have submitted' should be 'has submitted' — 'each' is singular
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'Each student has submitted'.

questions.question: 'When Ama met Abena, she gave her a book.' — What is the grammar problem?
options: Ambiguous pronoun reference — unclear whether 'she' refers to Ama or Abena
The sentence should not have two names
questions.answer: Ambiguous pronoun reference — unclear whether 'she' refers to Ama or Abena
questions.explanation: Ambiguous pronoun reference occurs when a pronoun could refer to more than one antecedent.

questions.question: What is a COMMA SPLICE?
options: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma: 'I was tired, I went to sleep.'
Using a comma before 'and' in a list
Placing a comma after an introductory phrase
questions.answer: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma: 'I was tired, I went to sleep.'
questions.explanation: Fix by adding a conjunction or using a semicolon.

questions.question: 'The clever student quickly answered the difficult question.' — Identify the ADVERB.
questions.answer: quickly
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'answered'.

questions.question: Which sentence is the MOST clear and effective?
options: The boy who was very very tired in a very extreme way went to sleep.
He slept because he was tired in many ways.
Going to sleep was done by the tired boy.
questions.answer: The exhausted boy fell asleep.
questions.explanation: Effective sentences are clear, concise, and precise.

questions.question: 'Good communication skills helps you to succeed in school, work, and life.' What is the error?
options: 'Skills helps' should be 'skills help' — 'skills' is plural
'School, work, and life' should not be listed together
questions.answer: 'Skills helps' should be 'skills help' — 'skills' is plural
questions.explanation: Subject-verb agreement: plural 'skills' requires plural verb 'help'.
